**Bottom Line**
No. In 2024 Hasina’s government did not protect independent media or open information access. The evidence instead points to blocking news sites, throttling internet/communications, arresting critics for speech, and using shutdowns/censorship to suppress scrutiny during both the election period and the July crisis. I found no reliable positive 2024 evidence of meaningful protection for independent journalism.

- **Bangladesh: Freedom on the Net 2024 Country Report** — Freedom House — 2024 — https://freedomhouse.org/country/bangladesh/freedom-net/2024 — Freedom House says the Awami League “manipulated the online information environment” ahead of the January 2024 election, including blocking major news sites and throttling internet/communications around BNP rallies. That is direct evidence of censorship and pressure on information access, not protection. `4B.6`, `4B.2`, `4B.3`, `4B.5`, `3B.8`, `3B.9`

- **Bangladesh: Freedom in the World 2024 Country Report** — Freedom House — 2024 — https://freedomhouse.org/country/bangladesh/freedom-world/2024 — Freedom House says the Awami League consolidated power through harassment of the BNP and critical media. It also says the ruling party used coercive economic power via state resources and that the media/electoral environment was politicized. This is strong evidence against protecting independent media and information access. `4B.6`, `4B.2`, `4B.3`, `4B.5`, `4B.4`

- **Bangladesh repression, security force abuses discredit elections** — Human Rights Watch — January 11, 2024 — https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/01/11/bangladesh-repression-security-force-abuses-discredit-elections — HRW reported arrests for criticism, including social-media posts, plus repression and violence against opposition members before the January election. This shows the state was chilling speech and press-adjacent criticism rather than protecting independent information flows. `4B.6`, `4B.3`, `4B.5`, `4B.1`

- **Little election fizz in Bangladesh as prime minister set for another term** — Reuters — January 4, 2024 — https://theprint.in/world/little-election-fizz-in-bangladesh-as-prime-minister-set-for-another-term/1910693/ — Reuters reported the opposition boycott followed Hasina’s refusal to resign and allow a neutral authority to run the election. This supports the broader picture of a controlled information and political environment, not one that protected independent scrutiny. `4B.6`, `4B.2`, `4B.4`, `4B.5`, `4B.1`

- **Bangladesh army enforces curfew as student-led protests spiral** — Reuters — July 20, 2024 — https://theprint.in/world/bangladesh-army-enforces-curfew-as-student-led-protests-spiral/2182818/ — Reuters described soldiers in Dhaka, roadblocks, and internet/text shutdowns during the crackdown. That is direct evidence of censorship and suppression of information access in a domestic crisis. `4B.6`, `3B.8`, `3B.9`, `4B.3`

- **Bangladesh’s crackdown left more than 170 dead, U.N. says** — UN/OHCHR — July 26, 2024 — https://bangladesh.un.org/en/275065-bangladesh-t%C3%BCrk-decries-government-crackdown-urges-respect-international-human-rights — The UN said more than 170 people were killed and warned that internet shutdowns increase impunity. That corroborates that information restrictions were being used to reduce scrutiny rather than protect independent media. `4B.6`, `3B.8`, `3B.9`, `4B.3`, `4B.4`

- **Bangladesh turnout low in election set to keep PM Hasina in power** — Reuters — January 7, 2024 — https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/bangladesh-turnout-low-in-election-set-to-keep-pm-hasina-in-power-3268699 — Reuters described the election as one set to keep Hasina in power, with the main opposition boycotting and turnout low. This reinforces the broader environment of controlled information and contested legitimacy. `4B.6`, `4B.1`, `4B.2`

**Search Gap**
I did not find reliable 2024 evidence that Hasina protected independent media owners, journalists, or open access to information. The evidence base is overwhelmingly negative. The only weak counterevidence in adjacent questions is reactive de-escalation after coercive shutdowns ended, but that is not evidence of pro-media protection.
